passages.text: Then Job answered: “Listen carefully to my words; let this be your consolation to me.
passages.sermon:
Job spoke.
Job answered his friends.
He said, "Listen to my words."
He told them, "Pay close attention."
He said, "Let my words be your comfort to me."
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ שִׁמְע֣וּ שָׁ֭מוֹעַ מִלָּתִ֑י וּתְהִי־ זֹ֝֗את תַּנְח֥וּמֹֽתֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Bear with me while I speak; then, after I have spoken, you may go on mocking.
passages.sermon:
Job is speaking to his friends.
Job asks his friends to listen to him.
He says, "Let me speak."
He says, "Be patient with me while I talk."
He says, "After I finish speaking, you may mock me."
He gives his friends permission to respond after he is done.
passages.original: שָׂ֭אוּנִי וְאָנֹכִ֣י אֲדַבֵּ֑ר וְאַחַ֖ר דַּבְּרִ֣י תַלְעִֽיג׃

passages.text: Is my complaint against a man? Then why should I not be impatient?
passages.sermon:
Job is speaking.
\r\nJob is suffering.
\r\nJob asks a question.
\r\nJob says, “Is my complaint directed at a man?”
\r\nJob’s complaint is not against a human.
\r\nJob asks, “Why should I not be impatient?”
\r\nJob feels justified in his impatience.
passages.original: הֶ֭אָנֹכִי לְאָדָ֣ם שִׂיחִ֑י וְאִם־ מַ֝דּ֗וּעַ לֹא־ תִקְצַ֥ר רוּחִֽי׃

passages.text: Look at me and be appalled; put your hand over your mouth.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
He suffers greatly.
He asks them to look at him.
He tells them to be shocked.
He commands them to cover their mouths with their hands.
passages.original: פְּנוּ־ אֵלַ֥י וְהָשַׁ֑מּוּ וְשִׂ֖ימוּ יָ֣ד עַל־ פֶּֽה׃

passages.text: When I remember, terror takes hold, and my body trembles in horror.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks about his suffering.
He remembers his pain.
He feels afraid.
Terror grips him.
His body shakes with horror.
passages.original: וְאִם־ זָכַ֥רְתִּי וְנִבְהָ֑לְתִּי וְאָחַ֥ז בְּ֝שָׂרִ֗י פַּלָּצֽוּת׃

passages.text: Why do the wicked live on, growing old and increasing in power?
passages.sermon:
The wicked are people who do evil.
They continue to live.
They grow old.
They become strong.
They gain more power.
passages.original: מַדּ֣וּעַ רְשָׁעִ֣ים יִחְי֑וּ עָ֝תְק֗וּ גַּם־ גָּ֥בְרוּ חָֽיִל׃

passages.text: Their descendants are established around them, and their offspring before their eyes.
passages.sermon:
The wicked have children.
Their children remain with them.
Their descendants stand secure before them.
Their offspring live where they can see them.
passages.original: זַרְעָ֤ם נָכ֣וֹן לִפְנֵיהֶ֣ם עִמָּ֑ם וְ֝צֶאֱצָאֵיהֶ֗ם לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Their homes are safe from fear; no rod of punishment from God is upon them.
passages.sermon:
The wicked live in safety.
Their homes have peace.
They do not fear danger.
God does not punish them.
No rod from God strikes them.
passages.original: בָּתֵּיהֶ֣ם שָׁל֣וֹם מִפָּ֑חַד וְלֹ֤א שֵׁ֖בֶט אֱל֣וֹהַּ עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Their bulls breed without fail; their cows bear calves and do not miscarry.
passages.sermon:
The people in this passage are prosperous and secure.
Their bulls breed successfully.
Their bulls do not fail to produce offspring.
Their cows give birth to calves.
Their cows do not miscarry.
passages.original: שׁוֹר֣וֹ עִ֭בַּר וְלֹ֣א יַגְעִ֑ל תְּפַלֵּ֥ט פָּ֝רָת֗וֹ וְלֹ֣א תְשַׁכֵּֽל׃

passages.text: They send forth their little ones like a flock; their children skip about, singing to the tambourine and lyre and making merry at the sound of the flute.
passages.sermon:
These people are prosperous and secure.
They send out their little ones like a flock of sheep.
Their children skip and play.
Their children sing to the tambourine and the lyre.
Their children rejoice at the sound of the flute.
passages.original: יְשַׁלְּח֣וּ כַ֭צֹּאן עֲוִילֵיהֶ֑ם וְ֝יַלְדֵיהֶ֗ם יְרַקֵּדֽוּן׃ יִ֭שְׂאוּ כְּתֹ֣ף וְכִנּ֑וֹר וְ֝יִשְׂמְח֗וּ לְק֣וֹל עוּגָֽב׃

passages.text: They spend their days in prosperity and go down to Sheol in peace.
passages.sermon:
These people live in prosperity.
They enjoy good things throughout their lives.
They do not suffer during their days.
When they die, they go down to Sheol.
They go to the grave quickly and peacefully.
passages.original: יְבַלּוּ בַטּ֣וֹב יְמֵיהֶ֑ם וּ֝בְרֶ֗גַע שְׁא֣וֹל יֵחָֽתּוּ׃

passages.text: Yet they say to God: ‘Leave us alone! For we have no desire to know Your ways.
passages.sermon:
Wicked people speak to God.
They say, “Go away from us.”
They do not want God near them.
They do not want to know God’s ways.
They have no desire to learn from God.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לָ֭אֵל ס֣וּר מִמֶּ֑נּוּ וְדַ֥עַת דְּ֝רָכֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א חָפָֽצְנוּ׃

passages.text: Who is the Almighty, that we should serve Him, and what would we gain if we pray to Him?’
passages.sermon:
Some people speak to God.
They say, “Who is the Almighty?”
They do not know God’s power.
They ask, “Why should we serve Him?”
They do not want to obey God.
They ask, “What benefit is there if we pray to Him?”
They do not believe prayer helps them.
They do not see value in worshiping God.
passages.original: מַה־ שַׁדַּ֥י כִּֽי־ נַֽעַבְדֶ֑נּוּ וּמַה־ נּ֝וֹעִ֗יל כִּ֣י נִפְגַּע־ בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Still, their prosperity is not in their own hands, so I stay far from the counsel of the wicked.
passages.sermon:
The wicked are people who reject God.
They do not want to know God’s ways.
They tell God to leave them alone.
They do not control their own prosperity.
Their success does not come from their own power.
I do not follow the advice of the wicked.
I keep far away from their counsel.
passages.original: הֵ֤ן לֹ֣א בְיָדָ֣ם טוּבָ֑ם עֲצַ֥ת רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים רָ֣חֲקָה מֶֽנִּי׃

passages.text: How often is the lamp of the wicked put out? Does disaster come upon them? Does God, in His anger, apportion destruction?
passages.sermon:
The wicked are people who do evil.
Their lives are like a lamp.
Sometimes, the lamp of the wicked goes out.
Sometimes, disaster comes upon them.
God can become angry.
God can give them destruction when He is angry.
God decides when to punish the wicked.
passages.original: כַּמָּ֤ה׀ נֵר־ רְשָׁ֘עִ֤ים יִדְעָ֗ךְ וְיָבֹ֣א עָלֵ֣ימוֹ אֵידָ֑ם חֲ֝בָלִ֗ים יְחַלֵּ֥ק בְּאַפּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Are they like straw before the wind, like chaff swept away by a storm?
passages.sermon:
The wicked are powerless before God.
They are like straw in front of the wind.
A strong wind blows the straw away.
They are like chaff taken by a storm.
A storm sweeps the chaff away quickly.
The wicked cannot stand against God’s power.
passages.original: יִהְי֗וּ כְּתֶ֥בֶן לִפְנֵי־ ר֑וּחַ וּ֝כְמֹ֗ץ גְּנָבַ֥תּוּ סוּפָֽה׃

passages.text: It is said that God lays up one’s punishment for his children. Let God repay the man himself, so he will know it.
passages.sermon:
God is the judge.
Some people say God saves a man's punishment for his children.
Let God repay the man himself.
Then the man will know it.
passages.original: אֱל֗וֹהַּ יִצְפֹּן־ לְבָנָ֥יו אוֹנ֑וֹ יְשַׁלֵּ֖ם אֵלָ֣יו וְיֵדָֽע׃

passages.text: Let his eyes see his own destruction; let him drink for himself the wrath of the Almighty.
passages.sermon: The man sees his own destruction with his eyes.\r\nHe drinks the wrath of the Almighty himself.
passages.original: יִרְא֣וּ עֵינוֹ כִּיד֑וֹ וּמֵחֲמַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י יִשְׁתֶּֽה׃

passages.text: For what does he care about his household after him, when the number of his months has run out?
passages.sermon:
A man dies when his time on earth ends.
He cannot add more months to his life.
After he dies, he leaves his household behind.
He does not care about his family after he is gone.
He has no concern for what happens to them after his death.
passages.original: כִּ֤י מַה־ חֶפְצ֣וֹ בְּבֵית֣וֹ אַחֲרָ֑יו וּמִסְפַּ֖ר חֳדָשָׁ֣יו חֻצָּֽצוּ׃

passages.text: Can anyone teach knowledge to God, since He judges those on high?
passages.sermon:
God knows everything.
No one can teach God knowledge.
God judges those who are high and powerful.
God is the judge over all.
passages.original: הַלְאֵ֥ל יְלַמֶּד־ דָּ֑עַת וְ֝ה֗וּא רָמִ֥ים יִשְׁפּֽוֹט׃

passages.text: One man dies full of vigor, completely secure and at ease.
passages.sermon:
This man dies.
He is strong and healthy.
He feels safe.
He feels calm.
He has no fear.
He is at peace.
passages.original: זֶ֗ה יָ֭מוּת בְּעֶ֣צֶם תֻּמּ֑וֹ כֻּ֝לּ֗וֹ שַׁלְאֲנַ֥ן וְשָׁלֵֽיו׃

passages.text: His body is well nourished, and his bones are rich with marrow.
passages.sermon:
This man’s body is strong.
His body has plenty of nourishment.
His bones are full of marrow.
He is healthy and well-fed.
passages.original: עֲ֭טִינָיו מָלְא֣וּ חָלָ֑ב וּמֹ֖חַ עַצְמוֹתָ֣יו יְשֻׁקֶּֽה׃

passages.text: Yet another man dies in the bitterness of his soul, having never tasted prosperity.
passages.sermon:
Another man dies.
His soul feels bitter.
He never enjoyed good things.
He never experienced prosperity.
passages.original: וְזֶ֗ה יָ֭מוּת בְּנֶ֣פֶשׁ מָרָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־ אָ֝כַ֗ל בַּטּוֹבָֽה׃

passages.text: But together they lie down in the dust, and worms cover them both.
passages.sermon: All people die.\r\nThey lie down together in the dust.\r\nWorms cover their bodies.
passages.original: יַ֭חַד עַל־ עָפָ֣ר יִשְׁכָּ֑בוּ וְ֝רִמָּ֗ה תְּכַסֶּ֥ה עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Behold, I know your thoughts full well, the schemes by which you would wrong me.
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
He knows their thoughts.
He understands their plans.
They plan to harm him.
They scheme against him.
passages.original: הֵ֣ן יָ֭דַעְתִּי מַחְשְׁבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וּ֝מְזִמּ֗וֹת עָלַ֥י תַּחְמֹֽסוּ׃

passages.text: For you say, ‘Where now is the nobleman’s house, and where are the tents in which the wicked dwell?’
passages.sermon: You ask a question.\r\nYou say, “Where is the house of the nobleman?”\r\nYou also say, “Where are the tents where wicked people live?”
passages.original: כִּ֤י תֹֽאמְר֗וּ אַיֵּ֥ה בֵית־ נָדִ֑יב וְ֝אַיֵּ֗ה אֹ֤הֶל׀ מִשְׁכְּנ֬וֹת רְשָׁעִֽים׃

passages.text: Have you never asked those who travel the roads? Do you not accept their reports?
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
Job knows his friends question him.
Job asks his friends a question.
He says, "Have you asked travelers?"
Travelers walk along the road.
Travelers see many things.
Job asks, "Do you not accept what travelers report?"
Travelers can give true reports.
Job wants his friends to listen to these reports.
passages.original: הֲלֹ֣א שְׁ֭אֶלְתֶּם ע֣וֹבְרֵי דָ֑רֶךְ וְ֝אֹתֹתָ֗ם לֹ֣א תְנַכֵּֽרוּ׃

passages.text: Indeed, the evil man is spared from the day of calamity, delivered from the day of wrath.
passages.sermon:
The evil man lives.
He does not suffer on the day of disaster.
He escapes when anger and punishment come.
God does not punish him on the day of wrath.
He is kept safe from trouble.
passages.original: כִּ֤י לְי֣וֹם אֵ֭יד יֵחָ֣שֶׂךְ רָ֑ע לְי֖וֹם עֲבָר֣וֹת יוּבָֽלוּ׃

passages.text: Who denounces his behavior to his face? Who repays him for what he has done?
passages.sermon:
No one tells the evil man to his face what he has done.
No one confronts him about his actions.
No one pays him back for what he has done.
No one holds him accountable for his deeds.
passages.original: מִֽי־ יַגִּ֣יד עַל־ פָּנָ֣יו דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וְהֽוּא־ עָ֝שָׂ֗ה מִ֣י יְשַׁלֶּם־ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He is carried to the grave, and watch is kept over his tomb.
passages.sermon: The evil man dies.\r\nPeople carry him to his grave.\r\nSomeone watches over his tomb.
passages.original: וְ֭הוּא לִקְבָר֣וֹת יוּבָ֑ל וְֽעַל־ גָּדִ֥ישׁ יִשְׁקֽוֹד׃

passages.text: The clods of the valley are sweet to him; everyone follows behind him, and those before him are without number.
passages.sermon:
This verse describes a wicked man after his death.
The soil in the valley feels pleasant to him.
Many people come after him.
Countless people went before him.
passages.original: מָֽתְקוּ־ ל֗וֹ רִגְבֵ֫י נָ֥חַל וְ֭אַחֲרָיו כָּל־ אָדָ֣ם יִמְשׁ֑וֹךְ וּ֝לְפָנָ֗יו אֵ֣ין מִסְפָּֽר׃

passages.text: So how can you comfort me with empty words? For your answers remain full of falsehood.”
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to his friends.
Job says their words do not help him.
Job calls their words empty.
Job says their answers are false.
Job says their comfort is useless.
passages.original: וְ֭אֵיךְ תְּנַחֲמ֣וּנִי הָ֑בֶל וּ֝תְשֽׁוּבֹתֵיכֶ֗ם נִשְׁאַר־ מָֽעַל׃ס
